claim: Allergic contact dermatitis (ACD) is affecting 15–20% of the world population.
source: Allergic contact dermatitis (ACD), one of the most common skin inflammatory diseases, is affecting 15–20% of the world population (Vocanson et al., 2009).
evidence: Supported by citation to Vocanson et al., 2009

claim: ACD is a delayed-type hypersensitivity reaction triggered by repeated skin contact with protein-reactive chemicals with low molecular weight.
source: It is a delayed-type hypersensitivity reaction triggered by repeated skin contact with protein-reactive chemicals with low molecular weight, such as haptens.
evidence: Established scientific knowledge about ACD pathophysiology

claim: A typical hapten-induced ACD reaction involves a sensitization phase, followed by an elicitation phase.
source: A typical hapten-induced ACD reaction involves a sensitization phase, followed by an elicitation phase.
evidence: Established scientific knowledge about ACD pathophysiology

claim: In the sensitization phase, high doses of low-molecular-weight haptens (<500 Da) penetrate through the skin stratum corneum and are captured by Langerhans cells and dendritic cells.
source: In the sensitization phase, high doses of low-molecular-weight haptens (<500 Da) penetrate through the skin stratum corneum and are captured by Langerhans cells and dendritic cells, which process these antigens and present them to naïve T cells in the skin-draining lymph nodes, priming and clonally expanding the hapten-specific T cells systemically (Kaplan et al., 2012).
evidence: Supported by citation to Kaplan et al., 2012

claim: In the elicitation phase, skin re-exposure to haptens triggers the activation of hapten-specific T cells and a cascade of inflammatory reactions, generally 24–72 hr after exposure.
source: In the elicitation phase, skin re-exposure to haptens (even at low doses) triggers the activation of hapten-specific T cells and a cascade of inflammatory reactions, generally, 24–72 hr after exposure (Manresa, 2021).
evidence: Supported by citation to Manresa, 2021

claim: Hapten-triggered innate immune response involves the release of proinflammatory cytokines and/or chemokines, such as IL1β, TNFα, CXCL9/10, CCL17, and CCL20.
source: Hapten-triggered innate immune response involves the release of a panel of proinflammatory cytokines and/or chemokines, such as IL1β, TNFα, CXCL9/10, CCL17, and CCL20, which contribute to T cell trafficking to the skin (Kaplan et al., 2012; Meller et al., 2007; Dufour et al., 2002).
evidence: Supported by citations to Kaplan et al., 2012; Meller et al., 2007; Dufour et al., 2002

claim: CD8+ T cells are considered the main effector cells in ACD.
source: Both CD4+ and CD8+ T cells are involved in inflammatory responses, and CD8+ T cells are considered the main effector cells (Chai et al., 2022; Vocanson et al., 2006).
evidence: Supported by citations to Chai et al., 2022; Vocanson et al., 2006

claim: Dermal fibroblasts are highly heterogeneous and can be classified based on their anatomical location.
source: Dermal fibroblasts (dFBs), the main resident cell type in skin dermis, are highly heterogeneous, and can be classified based on their anatomical location (Huang et al., 2022).
evidence: Supported by citation to Huang et al., 2022

claim: The development of skin erythema and thickening peaked at ~24 hr and lasted until ~60 hr post-treatment in the DNFB-elicited ACD mouse model.
source: The development of skin erythema and thickening peaked at ~24 hr and lasted until ~60 hr post-treatment (p.t.) (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A and B).
evidence: Supported by experimental observations shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1A and B

claim: The skin dermis drastically expanded at 24 hr post-treatment, and the dermis became heavily infiltrated with mononuclear cells by 60 hr post-treatment.
source: Histological analyses showed that the skin dermis drastically expanded at 24 hr p.t., and the dermis became heavily infiltrated with mononuclear cells by 60 hr p.t. (Figure 1—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: Supported by histological data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1C

claim: Single-cell RNA-seq identified up to 30 cell clusters in control and ACD ear skin samples.
source: To characterize the cell type-specific immune responses in this DNFB-elicited mouse ACD model, we performed scRNA-seq of control and ACD ear skin samples, and identified up to 30 cell clusters (Figure 1B), which were grouped into several cell types, including chondrocytes, dermal fibroblasts, keratinocytes, T cells, myeloid cells (basophils/BFs, mast cells/MCs, macrophages/MACs, neutrophils/NEUs, monocytes/Mon) and other skin resident cells based on marker gene expression (Figure 1C, Figure 1—figure supplement 1D, and Supplementary file 2).
evidence: Supported by scRNA-seq data shown in Figure 1B, 1C, and Figure 1—figure supplement 1D

claim: Lymphocytes and myeloid cells were the main cell types recruited to the skin after elicitation of ACD.
source: Furthermore, differential cell distribution plots (Figure 1D) showed that lymphocytes and myeloid cells were the main cell types recruited to the skin after elicitation of ACD (Figure 1E).
evidence: Supported by scRNA-seq data shown in Figure 1D and 1E

claim: Ifng, Il17, and Il10 were primarily expressed by T cell sub-clusters in ACD.
source: scRNA-seq gene expression plots revealed that Ifng, Il17, and Il10 were primarily expressed by T cell sub-clusters as expected; to our surprise, Il4 and Il13 were primarily produced by basophils, and Il1b was detected at the highest levels in the neutrophil/monocyte cluster and at intermediate levels in other myeloid cells, including basophils and macrophages (Figure 1G, Figure 1—figure supplement 1G).
evidence: Supported by scRNA-seq gene expression data shown in Figure 1G and Figure 1—figure supplement 1G

claim: Il4 and Il13 were primarily produced by basophils in ACD.
source: scRNA-seq gene expression plots revealed that Ifng, Il17, and Il10 were primarily expressed by T cell sub-clusters as expected; to our surprise, Il4 and Il13 were primarily produced by basophils, and Il1b was detected at the highest levels in the neutrophil/monocyte cluster and at intermediate levels in other myeloid cells, including basophils and macrophages (Figure 1G, Figure 1—figure supplement 1G).
evidence: Supported by scRNA-seq gene expression data shown in Figure 1G and Figure 1—figure supplement 1G

claim: Il1b was detected at the highest levels in the neutrophil/monocyte cluster in ACD.
source: scRNA-seq gene expression plots revealed that Ifng, Il17, and Il10 were primarily expressed by T cell sub-clusters as expected; to our surprise, Il4 and Il13 were primarily produced by basophils, and Il1b was detected at the highest levels in the neutrophil/monocyte cluster and at intermediate levels in other myeloid cells, including basophils and macrophages (Figure 1G, Figure 1—figure supplement 1G).
evidence: Supported by scRNA-seq gene expression data shown in Figure 1G and Figure 1—figure supplement 1G

claim: The expression of Ifng, but not Il4 or Il17a, was rapidly induced in skin draining lymph nodes at 24 hr after ACD elicitation.
source: Furthermore, we found that the expression of Ifng, but not Il4 or Il17a, was rapidly induced in skin draining lymph nodes at 24 hr after ACD elicitation (Figure 1—figure supplement 1H).
evidence: Supported by qRT-PCR data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1H

claim: T cell clusters were re-grouped into eight clusters defined as CD8+, CD4+, Treg, δγT, NKT, NK/ILC1, and ILC2.
source: To further define the T cell-specific immune response in ACD, T cell clusters were re-grouped into eight clusters (r0~r7; Figure 2A), which were defined as CD8+, CD4+, Treg, δγT, NKT, NK/ILC1, and ILC2, based on marker gene expression (Figure 2—figure supplement 1A and B).
evidence: Supported by scRNA-seq data shown in Figure 2A and Figure 2—figure supplement 1A and B

claim: ACD led to a notable increase in the percentage of CD8+, CD4+, Treg, and NK/ILC1 cells.
source: ACD led to a notable increase in the percentage of CD8+, CD4+, Treg, and NK/ILC1, but not in that of δγT and ILC2 cells (Figure 2B).
evidence: Supported by scRNA-seq data shown in Figure 2B

claim: In ACD skin, CD4+ and CD8+ T cells predominantly expressed marker genes associated with central memory T cells (Tcm).
source: We observed that in ACD skin, CD4+ and CD8+ T cells predominantly expressed marker genes associated with Tcm including Cd28, Cd27, Ccr7, and S1pr1/Cd62l. In contrast, marker genes associated with Tem (Cx3cr1) and Trm (Itga1/Cd49a, Itgae/Cd103, Cd69 and Prdm1/Blimp1, Cd127/Il7r) were only scarcely expressed in these αβ T cells (Figure 2—figure supplement 1C–D).
evidence: Supported by scRNA-seq data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1C–D

claim: ACD predominantly triggers a central memory T cell response in the skin.
source: These results suggest that ACD predominantly triggers a central memory T cell response in the skin.
evidence: Inferred from the observation that CD4+ and CD8+ T cells predominantly expressed Tcm markers

claim: Ifng was robustly induced in CD4+, CD8+, and NK/ILC1 T cell clusters in ACD.
source: Furthermore, gene expression plots (Figure 2C–D and Figure 2—figure supplement 1C) showed that Ifng was robustly induced in CD4+, CD8+, and NK/ILC1 T cell clusters, whereas Il10 and Il17a were moderately induced only in the Treg and δγT (r5) cell clusters, respectively.
evidence: Supported by scRNA-seq gene expression data shown in Figure 2C–D and Figure 2—figure supplement 1C

claim: Il10 was moderately induced only in the Treg cell cluster in ACD.
source: Furthermore, gene expression plots (Figure 2C–D and Figure 2—figure supplement 1C) showed that Ifng was robustly induced in CD4+, CD8+, and NK/ILC1 T cell clusters, whereas Il10 and Il17a were moderately induced only in the Treg and δγT (r5) cell clusters, respectively.
evidence: Supported by scRNA-seq gene expression data shown in Figure 2C–D and Figure 2—figure supplement 1C

claim: Il17a was moderately induced only in the δγT (r5) cell cluster in ACD.
source: Furthermore, gene expression plots (Figure 2C–D and Figure 2—figure supplement 1C) showed that Ifng was robustly induced in CD4+, CD8+, and NK/ILC1 T cell clusters, whereas Il10 and Il17a were moderately induced only in the Treg and δγT (r5) cell clusters, respectively.
evidence: Supported by scRNA-seq gene expression data shown in Figure 2C–D and Figure 2—figure supplement 1C

claim: Il4 was barely detectable in all T cell subsets in ACD.
source: In contrast, Il4 was barely detectable in all T cell subsets.
evidence: Supported by scRNA-seq gene expression analysis

claim: Chemokine signaling and type II interferon signaling pathways were among the top upregulated pathways in CD4+ and CD8+ T cells in ACD.
source: GO pathway analysis of CD4+ and CD8+ T cell clusters revealed that chemokine signaling and type II interferon signaling pathways were among the top upregulated, and TGFβ and PI3K-Akt-mTOR signaling were among the top downregulated pathways in ACD compared control (Figure 2E).
evidence: Supported by GO pathway analysis shown in Figure 2E

claim: TGFβ and PI3K-Akt-mTOR signaling were among the top downregulated pathways in CD4+ and CD8+ T cells in ACD.
source: GO pathway analysis of CD4+ and CD8+ T cell clusters revealed that chemokine signaling and type II interferon signaling pathways were among the top upregulated, and TGFβ and PI3K-Akt-mTOR signaling were among the top downregulated pathways in ACD compared control (Figure 2E).
evidence: Supported by GO pathway analysis shown in Figure 2E

claim: Ifng and several IFN-JAK-STAT-related genes (including Ifitm1/2/3 and Stat1) were among the top upregulated genes in CD4+ and CD8+ T cells in ACD.
source: Volcano plot of differentially expressed genes (Figure 2F) showed that Ifng and several IFN-JAK-STAT-related genes (including Ifitm1/2/3 and Stat1) were among the top upregulated genes in ACD, and genes with reported inhibitory functions for T cell activation and/or Th1 polarization, including Fos (Xiao et al., 2012), Zfp36 (Moore et al., 2018), and Klf4 (An et al., 2011), were among the top downregulated genes in ACD, compared to those in the control.
evidence: Supported by differential gene expression analysis shown in Figure 2F

claim: Genes with reported inhibitory functions for T cell activation and/or Th1 polarization, including Fos, Zfp36, and Klf4, were among the top downregulated genes in CD4+ and CD8+ T cells in ACD.
source: Volcano plot of differentially expressed genes (Figure 2F) showed that Ifng and several IFN-JAK-STAT-related genes (including Ifitm1/2/3 and Stat1) were among the top upregulated genes in ACD, and genes with reported inhibitory functions for T cell activation and/or Th1 polarization, including Fos (Xiao et al., 2012), Zfp36 (Moore et al., 2018), and Klf4 (An et al., 2011), were among the top downregulated genes in ACD, compared to those in the control.
evidence: Supported by differential gene expression analysis shown in Figure 2F and citations to Xiao et al., 2012; Moore et al., 2018; An et al., 2011

claim: DNFB-elicited ACD resulted in a rapid increase in both CD4+ and CD8+ T cells, in which IFNγ expression was significantly induced.
source: FACS analysis (Figure 2G and Figure 2—figure supplement 1H–K) showed that DNFB-elicited ACD resulted in a rapid increase in both CD4+ and CD8+ T cells, in which IFNγ expression was significantly induced, whereas IL4/IL13 and/or IL17 expression was inhibited.
evidence: Supported by FACS data shown in Figure 2G and Figure 2—figure supplement 1H–K

claim: IL4/IL13 and/or IL17 expression was inhibited in CD4+ and CD8+ T cells in ACD.
source: FACS analysis (Figure 2G and Figure 2—figure supplement 1H–K) showed that DNFB-elicited ACD resulted in a rapid increase in both CD4+ and CD8+ T cells, in which IFNγ expression was significantly induced, whereas IL4/IL13 and/or IL17 expression was inhibited.
evidence: Supported by FACS data shown in Figure 2G and Figure 2—figure supplement 1H–K

claim: T cells are primarily polarized to the IFNγ-producing type-1 inflammatory phenotype in DNFB-elicited ACD.
source: Together, these results indicate that T cells are primarily polarized to the IFNγ-producing type-1 inflammatory phenotype in DNFB-elicited ACD.
evidence: Inferred from multiple lines of evidence showing IFNγ induction and IL4/IL13/IL17 inhibition in T cells

claim: ACD led to an increase of basophils, mast cells, neutrophils, and macrophages.
source: scRNA-seq analysis of myeloid cell clusters showed that ACD led to an increase of basophils, mast cells, neutrophils, and macrophages (Figure 3A).
evidence: Supported by scRNA-seq data shown in Figure 3A

claim: Il4 was primarily expressed by basophils and mast cells in ACD.
source: Violin plot analyses of cytokines across major skin or immune cell types confirmed that Il4 was primarily expressed by basophils and mast cells, whereas Il1b was primarily expressed by neutrophils and macrophages (Figure 3B and Figure 3—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: Supported by scRNA-seq data shown in Figure 3B and Figure 3—figure supplement 1A

claim: Il1b was primarily expressed by neutrophils and macrophages in ACD.
source: Violin plot analyses of cytokines across major skin or immune cell types confirmed that Il4 was primarily expressed by basophils and mast cells, whereas Il1b was primarily expressed by neutrophils and macrophages (Figure 3B and Figure 3—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: Supported by scRNA-seq data shown in Figure 3B and Figure 3—figure supplement 1A

claim: Basophils expressed higher levels of cytokines/chemokines, such as Il4, Il13, and Il6, compared to mast cells in ACD.
source: Volcano plots of genes expressed by mast cells (Cd11b-Cma1+Fcer1a+) and basophils (Cd11b+Mcpt8+Fcer1a+) showed that, in comparison, basophils expressed higher levels of cytokines/chemokines, such as Il4, Il13, and Il6, and mast cells expressed higher levels of Ccl2 and Ccl7 (Figure 3C), revealing their differential immune responses in ACD.
evidence: Supported by differential gene expression analysis shown in Figure 3C

claim: Mast cells expressed higher levels of Ccl2 and Ccl7 compared to basophils in ACD.
source: Volcano plots of genes expressed by mast cells (Cd11b-Cma1+Fcer1a+) and basophils (Cd11b+Mcpt8+Fcer1a+) showed that, in comparison, basophils expressed higher levels of cytokines/chemokines, such as Il4, Il13, and Il6, and mast cells expressed higher levels of Ccl2 and Ccl7 (Figure 3C), revealing their differential immune responses in ACD.
evidence: Supported by differential gene expression analysis shown in Figure 3C

claim: The expression levels of Mcpt8 (BF marker), but not Cma1 (MC marker), were elevated in a time-dependent manner upon ACD-elicitation.
source: First, the expression levels of Mcpt8 (BF marker), but not Cma1 (MC marker), were elevated in a time-dependent manner upon ACD-elicitation (Figure 3D).
evidence: Supported by qRT-PCR data shown in Figure 3D

claim: ACD triggered a rapid increase in the percentage of IL4/IL13-producing CD11B+ FcεR1a+ basophils as early as 24 hr post-elicitation.
source: FACS analysis of BFs and MCs, based on the surface expression of CD11B and FcεR1a (Figure 3E and F and Figure 3—figure supplement 1B), showed that ACD triggered a rapid increase in the percentage of IL4/IL13-producing CD11B+ FcεR1a+ BFs as early as 24 hr post-elicitation.
evidence: Supported by FACS data shown in Figure 3E, 3F, and Figure 3—figure supplement 1B

claim: There was only a moderate and delayed increase in IL4/IL13-producing CD11B- FcεR1a+ mast cells after ACD-elicitation.
source: In contrast, there was only a moderate and delayed increase in IL4/IL13-producing CD11B- FcεR1a+ MCs after ACD-elicitation (Figure 3E and F).
evidence: Supported by FACS data shown in Figure 3E and 3F

claim: Elicitation of ACD led to dermal infiltration of both FcεR1a+ TPSB- basophils and FcεR1a+ TPSB+ mast cells, in which Th2 cytokines were primarily co-localized.
source: In addition, immunostaining analysis showed that elicitation of ACD led to dermal infiltration of both FcεR1a+ TPSB- BFs and FcεR1a+ TPSB+ MCs, in which Th2 cytokines were primarily co-localized (Figure 3—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: Supported by immunostaining data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1C

claim: S100a8/9, Il1b, and Cxcl2 were among the most highly expressed genes in the neutrophil/monocyte cell cluster in ACD.
source: Sc-RNAseq revealed that S100a8/9, Il1b, and Cxcl2 were among the most highly expressed genes in the neutrophil/monocyte cell cluster (Figure 3—figure supplement 1D), and Il1b was among the top inducible genes in Cd68+ + after ACD elicitation (Figure 3H).
evidence: Supported by scRNA-seq data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1D

claim: Il1b was among the top inducible genes in Cd68+ macrophages after ACD elicitation.
source: Sc-RNAseq revealed that S100a8/9, Il1b, and Cxcl2 were among the most highly expressed genes in the neutrophil/monocyte cell cluster (Figure 3—figure supplement 1D), and Il1b was among the top inducible genes in Cd68+ + after ACD elicitation (Figure 3H).
evidence: Supported by scRNA-seq data shown in Figure 3H

claim: Genes associated with immunosuppressive or M2 macrophages (Cd74, H2-Ab, and Ccl24) were among the most downregulated genes in macrophages after ACD elicitation.
source: Interestingly, genes associated with immunosuppressive or M2 MACs (Cd74, H2-Ab, and Ccl24) were among the most downregulated genes in MACs after ACD elicitation (Figure 3H).
evidence: Supported by scRNA-seq data shown in Figure 3H

claim: 'Cellular response to IFNγ' was the top upregulated pathway in macrophages after elicitation of ACD.
source: Furthermore, GO pathway analysis identified 'cellular response to IFNγ' as the top upregulated pathway, and 'lipid metabolic' and 'actin cytoskeleton organization' as the top downregulated pathways in MACs after elicitation of ACD (Figure 3I).
evidence: Supported by GO pathway analysis shown in Figure 3I

claim: 'Lipid metabolic' and 'actin cytoskeleton organization' were the top downregulated pathways in macrophages after elicitation of ACD.
source: Furthermore, GO pathway analysis identified 'cellular response to IFNγ' as the top upregulated pathway, and 'lipid metabolic' and 'actin cytoskeleton organization' as the top downregulated pathways in MACs after elicitation of ACD (Figure 3I).
evidence: Supported by GO pathway analysis shown in Figure 3I

claim: Elicitation of ACD led to a time-dependent increase in neutrophil recruitment.
source: FACS analysis of NEUs, monocytes, and MACs based on protocol reported by Rahman et al., 2017 confirmed that elicitation of ACD led to a time-dependent increase in NEU recruitment and a shift of MACs from a resting (Ly6Clo) to an inflammatory (Ly6Chi) state (Figure 3J–L and Figure 3—figure supplement 1E and F).
evidence: Supported by FACS data shown in Figure 3J–L and Figure 3—figure supplement 1E and F

claim: Elicitation of ACD led to a shift of macrophages from a resting (Ly6Clo) to an inflammatory (Ly6Chi) state.
source: FACS analysis of NEUs, monocytes, and MACs based on protocol reported by Rahman et al., 2017 confirmed that elicitation of ACD led to a time-dependent increase in NEU recruitment and a shift of MACs from a resting (Ly6Clo) to an inflammatory (Ly6Chi) state (Figure 3J–L and Figure 3—figure supplement 1E and F).
evidence: Supported by FACS data shown in Figure 3J–L and Figure 3—figure supplement 1E and F

claim: Elicitation of ACD led to a transient influx of monocytes peaking at 24 hr post treatment.
source: In contrast, elicitation of ACD led to a transient influx of monocytes peaking at 24 hr post treatment (Figure 3M, Figure 3—figure supplement 1G).
evidence: Supported by FACS data shown in Figure 3M and Figure 3—figure supplement 1G

claim: Pdgfra+ dermal fibroblasts were reclustered into seven sub-clusters (r0 to r6).
source: PDGFRA, a well-characterized skin pan-fibroblast marker (Lynch and Watt, 2018; Driskell et al., 2013), was used to identified dFBs, and Pdgfra+ dFBs were reclustered into seven sub-clusters (r0 to r6) (Figure 4A).
evidence: Supported by scRNA-seq data shown in Figure 4A

claim: The dermal fibroblast sub-clusters are defined as adipocyte progenitors (AP in r2), adipose regulatory cells (Areg in r6), preadipocytes (pAd, in r1 and r5), reticular/papillary dFBs (RET/PAP in r0), and peri-follicular dFBs (r4).
source: According to dFB and/or adipocyte-lineage cell marker gene profiles reported by our or others' work (Sun et al., 2023; Driskell et al., 2013; Plikus et al., 2021; Joost et al., 2020; Zachara et al., 2022; Schwalie et al., 2018), the dFB sub-clusters are defined as Mfap5+Dlk1+Ly6a+adipocyte progenitors (AP in r2), Fmo2+Ly6a+adipose regulatory cells (Areg in r6), Ly6a+Lpl+Apoe+Icam1+preadipocytes (pAd, in r1 and r5), Ly6alo or Lrig1+ + or papillary dFBs (RET/PAP in r0), and Ly6aloTrps1hi peri-follicular dFBs (including dermal papilla cells, r4; Figure 4B, Figure 4—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: Supported by marker gene expression shown in Figure 4B and Figure 4—figure supplement 1A, and citations to Sun et al., 2023; Driskell et al., 2013; Plikus et al., 2021; Joost et al., 2020; Zachara et al., 2022; Schwalie et al., 2018

claim: ACD elicitation led to an increase of the expression of IFN-inducible genes (Cxcl9, Cxcl10, Stat1) in the r5 preadipocyte cluster.
source: Bubble plots and violin plots showed that ACD elicitation led to an increase of the expression of a panel of IFN-inducible genes (Cxcl9, Cxcl10, Stat1), accompanied with a loss of the expression of pAd signature genes (Lpl, Apoe) and a panel of ECM genes (Col1a1, Col3a1) in the r5 pAd cluster (Figure 4C and Figure 4—figure supplement 1B and C).
evidence: Supported by scRNA-seq data shown in Figure 4C and Figure 4—figure supplement 1B and C

claim: ACD elicitation led to a loss of the expression of preadipocyte signature genes (Lpl, Apoe) and ECM genes (Col1a1, Col3a1) in the r5 preadipocyte cluster.
source: Bubble plots and violin plots showed that ACD elicitation led to an increase of the expression of a panel of IFN-inducible genes (Cxcl9, Cxcl10, Stat1), accompanied with a loss of the expression of pAd signature genes (Lpl, Apoe) and a panel of ECM genes (Col1a1, Col3a1) in the r5 pAd cluster (Figure 4C and Figure 4—figure supplement 1B and C).
evidence: Supported by scRNA-seq data shown in Figure 4C and Figure 4—figure supplement 1B and C

claim: The dFB_r5 cluster was specifically enriched with several transcription factors downstream of the interferon pathway (Stat1, Irf1, and Irf7).
source: In addition, scenic TF analysis revealed that the dFB_r5 cluster was specifically enriched with several TFs downstream of the interferon pathway (Stat1, Irf1, and Irf7; Figure 4D).
evidence: Supported by SCENIC TF analysis shown in Figure 4D

claim: Pathways including response to virus, cellular response to IFNγ, and positive regulation of T-cell-mediated cytotoxicity were among the top upregulated pathways in dFB_r5 cells in ACD.
source: Furthermore, GO pathway analysis of dFB_r5 cells showed that pathways including response to virus, cellular response to IFNγ, and positive regulation of T-cell-mediated cytotoxicity were among the top upregulated pathways, whereas ECM organization was among the top downregulated pathways in ACD compared to control (Figure 4E).
evidence: Supported by GO pathway analysis shown in Figure 4E

claim: ECM organization was among the top downregulated pathways in dFB_r5 cells in ACD.
source: Furthermore, GO pathway analysis of dFB_r5 cells showed that pathways including response to virus, cellular response to IFNγ, and positive regulation of T-cell-mediated cytotoxicity were among the top upregulated pathways, whereas ECM organization was among the top downregulated pathways in ACD compared to control (Figure 4E).
evidence: Supported by GO pathway analysis shown in Figure 4E

claim: Cxcl9, Cxcl10, Ccl2, Stat1, and other antiviral genes were the top upregulated genes in dFB_r5 cluster in ACD.
source: Accordingly, volcano gene expression plots of dFB_r5 cluster showed that Cxcl9, Cxcl10, Ccl2, Stat1, and other antiviral genes were the top upregulated genes, whereas ECM genes were the top downregulated genes in ACD compared to control (Figure 4F).
evidence: Supported by differential gene expression analysis shown in Figure 4F

claim: ECM genes were the top downregulated genes in dFB_r5 cluster in ACD.
source: Accordingly, volcano gene expression plots of dFB_r5 cluster showed that Cxcl9, Cxcl10, Ccl2, Stat1, and other antiviral genes were the top upregulated genes, whereas ECM genes were the top downregulated genes in ACD compared to control (Figure 4F).
evidence: Supported by differential gene expression analysis shown in Figure 4F

claim: Inflammatory genes related to the IFNGR pathway (Stat1, Cxcl9, Cxcl10) were expressed at highest levels in the dFB_r5 cluster.
source: Violin plots of major skin and immune cell types showed that inflammatory genes related to the IFNGR pathway (Stat1, Cxcl9, Cxcl10) were expressed at highest levels in the dFB_r5 cluster, whereas Ifng and Cxcr3 (receptor for CXCL9/10 ligands) was mainly expressed by T cells (Figure 4G and Figure 4—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: Supported by scRNA-seq data shown in Figure 4G and Figure 4—figure supplement 1D

claim: Ifng and Cxcr3 (receptor for CXCL9/10 ligands) was mainly expressed by T cells.
source: Violin plots of major skin and immune cell types showed that inflammatory genes related to the IFNGR pathway (Stat1, Cxcl9, Cxcl10) were expressed at highest levels in the dFB_r5 cluster, whereas Ifng and Cxcr3 (receptor for CXCL9/10 ligands) was mainly expressed by T cells (Figure 4G and Figure 4—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: Supported by scRNA-seq data shown in Figure 4G and Figure 4—figure supplement 1D

claim: CXCL9+ or CXCL10+ cells co-expressed PDGFRA in the lower dermis where PLIN1+ adipocytes are enriched of ACD skin samples.
source: Co-immunostaining analyses showed that CXCL9+ or CXCL10+ cells co-expressed PDGFRA in the lower dermis where PLIN1+ adipocytes are enriched of ACD skin samples (Figure 4H–J and Figure 4—figure supplement 1F–H), supporting that dFB is the major cell source for CXCL9/10 in ACD.
evidence: Supported by immunostaining data shown in Figure 4H–J and Figure 4—figure supplement 1F–H

claim: Dermal fibroblast is the major cell source for CXCL9/10 in ACD.
source: Co-immunostaining analyses showed that CXCL9+ or CXCL10+ cells co-expressed PDGFRA in the lower dermis where PLIN1+ adipocytes are enriched of ACD skin samples (Figure 4H–J and Figure 4—figure supplement 1F–H), supporting that dFB is the major cell source for CXCL9/10 in ACD.
evidence: Inferred from co-localization of CXCL9/10 with PDGFRA in immunostaining

claim: Phosphor-STAT1 (pSTAT1) was detected primarily in PDGFRA+Ly6A+ preadipocytes located within the lower dermis.
source: In addition, phosphor-STAT1 (pSTAT1), a key signaling molecule activated by IFNγ, was detected primarily in PDGFRA+Ly6A+ pAds located within the lower dermis (Figure 4—figure supplement 1I and J).
evidence: Supported by immunostaining data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1I and J

claim: In ACD skin dermis, CXCL9 expression largely co-localized with ICAM1.
source: Furthermore, in ACD skin dermis, CXCL9 expression largely co-localized with ICAM1 (Figure 4—figure supplement 1K), a marker for committed pAds (Merrick et al., 2019).
evidence: Supported by immunostaining data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1K and citation to Merrick et al., 2019

claim: CXCL9 is specifically induced in the preadipocyte subset of dermal fibroblasts.
source: This further confirms that CXCL9 is specifically induced in the pAd subset of dFBs.
evidence: Inferred from co-localization of CXCL9 with ICAM1, a preadipocyte marker

claim: The active ACD preadipocytes (dFB_r5) and the active IFNγ-responsive vitiligo dermal fibroblasts are enriched with highly similar IFNγ-inducible genes.
source: By comparing these active vitiligo mouse dFBs with the active ACD pAds (dFB_r5), we found that these two cell populations are enriched with highly similar IFNγ-inducible genes (Figure 5—figure supplement 1A and Supplementary file 3), suggesting that the IFNγ-responsive pAds may also contribute to the activation of type 1T cells in the context of ACD.
evidence: Supported by comparative analysis shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1A and Supplementary file 3

claim: Among all other dermal fibroblast clusters, the Pdgfra+Ly6A+Icam1+ dFB_r5 preadipocytes exhibited the highest expression levels of Ifngr1 and Ifngfr2, along with Stat1, Cxcl9, and Cxcl10.
source: First, violin plots showed that among all other dFB clusters, the Pdgfra +Ly6A+Icam1+dFB_r5 pAds exhibited the highest expression levels of Ifngr1 and Ifngfr2, along with Stat1, Cxcl9, and Cxcl10 (Figure 5—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: Supported by scRNA-seq data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1B

claim: Elicitation of ACD enabled IFNγ production from CD4+/CD8+ or ILC1/NK T cells, acting on IFNGR expressed on the dFB-r5 cluster.
source: Additionally, an unbiased IFNγ-IFNGR signaling network analysis revealed that elicitation of ACD enabled IFNγ production from CD4+/CD8+ or ILC1/NK T cells, acting on IFNGR expressed on the dFB-r5 cluster (Figure 5A).
evidence: Supported by cell-chat signaling network analysis shown in Figure 5A

claim: IFNγ uniquely upregulated the expression of a large pool of genes, including several antiviral- or IFNγ pathway-related genes in primary dermal fibroblasts.
source: Transcriptomic venn diagram analysis showed that IFNγ uniquely upregulated the expression of a large pool of genes, including several antiviral- or IFNγ pathway-related genes (Figure 5B–C and Supplementary files 4-5).
evidence: Supported by RNA-seq data shown in Figure 5B–C and Supplementary files 4-5

claim: IFNγ treatment robustly induced the expression of Cxcl9, Cxcl10, Stat1, and Ccl2 as early as 8 hr post-treatment in primary dermal fibroblasts.
source: Time course analysis showed that IFNγ treatment robustly induced the expression of Cxcl9, Cxcl10, Stat1, and Ccl2 as early as 8 hr post-treatment, and suppressed the expression of lipogenesis (Apoe) and ECM (Col1a1) genes in a delayed manner (Figure 5B and Figure 5—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: Supported by qRT-PCR data shown in Figure 5B and Figure 5—figure supplement 1C

claim: IFNγ treatment suppressed the expression of lipogenesis (Apoe) and ECM (Col1a1) genes in a delayed manner in primary dermal fibroblasts.
source: Time course analysis showed that IFNγ treatment robustly induced the expression of Cxcl9, Cxcl10, Stat1, and Ccl2 as early as 8 hr post-treatment, and suppressed the expression of lipogenesis (Apoe) and ECM (Col1a1) genes in a delayed manner (Figure 5B and Figure 5—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: Supported by qRT-PCR data shown in Figure 5B and Figure 5—figure supplement 1C

claim: Cxcr3 was specifically induced in T cells in ACD.
source: Additionally, Cxcr3 was specifically induced in T cells in ACD (Figure 5—figure supplement 1D), suggesting that IFNGR-dependent activation of dFBs may in turn promotes T cell recruitment/activation by producing CXCL9/10, which act on T cells via CXCR3.
evidence: Supported by scRNA-seq data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1D

claim: IFNγ-primed dermal fibroblasts secreted high level of CXCL10.
source: ELISA confirmed that IFNγ-primed dFBs secreted high level of CXCL10 (Figure 5F), and conditioned medium from unstimulated control or IFNγ-primed dFBs (dFBctrl-CM or dFBIFNγ-CM) was then added to primary lymphocytes with or without CD3/CD28-antibody costimulation.
evidence: Supported by ELISA data shown in Figure 5F

claim: In the absence of CD3/CD28 antibody, conditioned medium from IFNγ-primed dermal fibroblasts significantly enhanced IFNγ production from naïve T cells.
source: We found that in the absence of CD3/CD28 antibody, dFBIFNγ-CM significantly enhanced IFNγ production from naïve T cells, and blocking CXCR3 signaling by adding a CXCR3 neutralizing antibody inhibited this effect (Figure 5G).
evidence: Supported by ELISA data shown in Figure 5G

claim: Blocking CXCR3 signaling by adding a CXCR3 neutralizing antibody inhibited the effect of IFNγ-primed dermal fibroblast conditioned medium on IFNγ production from naïve T cells.
source: We found that in the absence of CD3/CD28 antibody, dFBIFNγ-CM significantly enhanced IFNγ production from naïve T cells, and blocking CXCR3 signaling by adding a CXCR3 neutralizing antibody inhibited this effect (Figure 5G).
evidence: Supported by ELISA data shown in Figure 5G

claim: In the presence of CD3/CD28 antibody, conditioned medium from control dermal fibroblasts inhibited IFNγ expression and promoted T cell polarization towards the IL4-producing type-2 phenotype.
source: Interestingly, in the presence of CD3/CD28 antibody, we found that compared to blank DMEM, dFBctrl-CM inhibited IFNγ expression and promoted T cell polarization towards the IL4-producing type-2 phenotype, whereas dFBIFNγ-CM downregulated IL4 expression and restored the ability of stimulated T cells to produce IFNγ (Figure 5H and Figure 5—figure supplement 1E).
evidence: Supported by ELISA data shown in Figure 5H and Figure 5—figure supplement 1E

claim: Conditioned medium from IFNγ-primed dermal fibroblasts downregulated IL4 expression and restored the ability of stimulated T cells to produce IFNγ.
source: Interestingly, in the presence of CD3/CD28 antibody, we found that compared to blank DMEM, dFBctrl-CM inhibited IFNγ expression and promoted T cell polarization towards the IL4-producing type-2 phenotype, whereas dFBIFNγ-CM downregulated IL4 expression and restored the ability of stimulated T cells to produce IFNγ (Figure 5H and Figure 5—figure supplement 1E).
evidence: Supported by ELISA data shown in Figure 5H and Figure 5—figure supplement 1E

claim: The effect of IFNγ-primed dermal fibroblast conditioned medium on T cell IFNγ production was partially reversed by adding a CXCR3 neutralizing antibody.
source: In addition, the effect dFBIFNγ-CM was partially reversed by adding a CXCR3 neutralizing antibody (Figure 5H and Figure 5—figure supplement 1E).
evidence: Supported by ELISA data shown in Figure 5H and Figure 5—figure supplement 1E

claim: IFNγ-primed dermal fibroblasts are capable to shift the T1/T2 polarization balance towards type-1 effector phenotype by activating the CXCR3 pathway during T cell activation.
source: These results indicate that IFNγ-primed dFBs are capable to shift the T1/T2 polarization balance towards type-1 effector phenotype by activating the CXCR3 pathway during T cell activation.
evidence: Inferred from in vitro co-culture experiments showing CXCR3-dependent effects

claim: Tamoxifen application to Ifngr1FB-iKO mice specifically ablated the expression of IFNGR1 in PDGFRA+ dermal fibroblasts, but not in other PDGFRA- dermal cells.
source: TAM application to Ifngr1FB-iKO mice specifically ablated the expression of IFNGR1 in PDGFRA+ dFBs, but not in other PDGFRA- dermal cells (Figure 6C and Figure 6—figure supplement 1A and B).
evidence: Supported by immunostaining data shown in Figure 6C and Figure 6—figure supplement 1A and B

claim: DNFB-mediated development of skin eczema was significantly inhibited in the Ifngr1FB-iKO mice.
source: As a result, DNFB-mediated development of skin eczema (Figure 6D and E), dermal cell infiltration (Figure 6F), induction of Cxcl9/10, Cxcr3, Ifng, Cd8a and other inflammatory genes (Figure 6G and Figure 6—figure supplement 1C), expression of CXCL9 in ICAM1+ pAds (Figure 6—figure supplement 1D–E), and dermal infiltration of CD8+ T cells (Figure 6 H and I) were significantly inhibited in the Ifngr1FB-iKO mice.
evidence: Supported by phenotypic and EASI score data shown in Figure 6D and E

claim: Dermal cell infiltration was significantly inhibited in the Ifngr1FB-iKO mice.

claim: Induction of Cxcl9/10, Cxcr3, Ifng, Cd8a and other inflammatory genes was significantly inhibited in the Ifngr1FB-iKO mice.
source: As a result, DNFB-mediated development of skin eczema (Figure 6D and E), dermal cell infiltration (Figure 6F), induction of Cxcl9/10, Cxcr3, Ifng, Cd8a and other inflammatory genes (Figure 6G and Figure 6—figure supplement 1C), expression of CXCL9 in ICAM1+ pAds (Figure 6—figure supplement 1D–E), and dermal infiltration of CD8+ T cells (Figure 6 H and I) were significantly inhibited in the Ifngr1FB-iKO mice.

evidence: Supported by immunostaining data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1D–E

claim: Dermal infiltration of CD8+ T cells was significantly inhibited in the Ifngr1FB-iKO mice.

claim: Targeted deletion of IFNγ receptor signaling in dermal fibroblasts inhibited the development of type-1 skin inflammation in ACD.
source: These results demonstrate that targeted deletion of IFNγ receptor signaling in dermal fibroblasts inhibited the development of type-1 skin inflammation in ACD.
evidence: Inferred from the phenotypic and molecular changes observed in Ifngr1FB-iKO mice

claim: Numerous CD8+ IFNγ+ T cells were present in the dermal micro-vascular structures in human ACD skin, but not in healthy control skin.
source: Co-immunostaining of IFNγ with CD4 and CD8 revealed that numerous CD8+ IFNγ+ T cells were present in the dermal micro-vascular structures, which are known to be enriched with mesenchymal stem cells (Russell-Goldman and Murphy, 2020), in ACD skin, but not in healthy control skin (Figure 7A, Figure 7—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: Supported by immunostaining data shown in Figure 7A and Figure 7—figure supplement 1A

claim: Within dermal micro-vascular structures, IFNγ was detected exclusively from CD8+ T cells in human ACD skin.
source: In addition, within these dermal structures, IFNγ was detected exclusively from CD8+ T cells (Figure 7B).
evidence: Supported by immunostaining intensity profile shown in Figure 7B

claim: CD8+ T cells are the major IFNγ-producing cells in the human ACD skin.
source: In contrast, infiltration of CD4+ T cells was not observed, suggesting that CD8+ T cells are the major IFNγ-producing cells in the human ACD skin.
evidence: Inferred from the observation that IFNγ was detected exclusively from CD8+ T cells and CD4+ T cell infiltration was not observed

claim: Collagen bundles were thinner and disorganized within the dermal micro-vascular structures where immune cells were heavily infiltrated in human ACD skin compared to healthy control skin.
source: In line with our mouse data, collagen bundles were thinner and disorganized within the dermal micro-vascular structures where immune cells were heavily infiltrated in human ACD skin compared to healthy control skin sections (Figure 7C).
evidence: Supported by Masson's staining shown in Figure 7C

claim: CD8+ T cells were infiltrated around the PDGFRA+ dermal fibroblasts within the dermal micro-vascular structure in human ACD skin.
source: Here, co-immunostaining of PDGFRA and CD8 revealed that CD8+ T cells were infiltrated around the PDGFRA+ dermal fibroblasts within the dermal micro-vascular structure in ACD skin (Figure 7D).
evidence: Supported by immunostaining data shown in Figure 7D

claim: PDGFRA+ dermal fibroblasts within dermal micro-vascular structures expressed CXCL10 in human ACD skin.
source: Furthermore, PDGFRA+ dermal fibroblasts within these micro-vascular structures expressed CXCL10 (Figure 7E and F, Figure 7—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: Supported by immunostaining data shown in Figure 7E, 7F, and Figure 7—figure supplement 1B

claim: The human dermal fibroblast population expressing CXCL10 correlated with the dFB-r5 cluster identified in the murine DNFB-elicited ACD skin.
source: This human dFB population correlated with the dFB-r5 cluster we identified in the murine DNFB-elicited ACD skin, in which Cxcl9/10 were strongly induced and collagen genes were inhibited.
evidence: Inferred from the similarity in CXCL10 expression and collagen changes between human and mouse ACD

claim: Infiltrated CD4+ or CD8+ lymphocytes were primarily the IFNγ-producing type 1 central memory phenotype upon elicitation of ACD.
source: Here, single-cell transcriptomic analysis of the murine hapten-elicited model of ACD reveals that upon elicitation of ACD, infiltrated CD4+ or CD8+ lymphocytes were primarily the IFNγ-producing type 1 central memory phenotype.
evidence: Supported by scRNA-seq analysis of T cell markers and cytokine expression

claim: Type 2 cytokines (IL4 and IL13) were dominantly expressed by basophils in ACD.
source: In contrast, type 2 cytokines (IL4 and IL13) were dominantly expressed by basophils, IL17A was primarily expressed by δγ T cells, and IL1β was identified as the primary cytokine expressed by activated neutrophils/monocytes and macrophages.
evidence: Supported by scRNA-seq analysis of cytokine expression across cell types

claim: IL17A was primarily expressed by δγ T cells in ACD.
source: In contrast, type 2 cytokines (IL4 and IL13) were dominantly expressed by basophils, IL17A was primarily expressed by δγ T cells, and IL1β was identified as the primary cytokine expressed by activated neutrophils/monocytes and macrophages.
evidence: Supported by scRNA-seq analysis of cytokine expression across cell types

claim: IL1β was identified as the primary cytokine expressed by activated neutrophils/monocytes and macrophages in ACD.
source: In contrast, type 2 cytokines (IL4 and IL13) were dominantly expressed by basophils, IL17A was primarily expressed by δγ T cells, and IL1β was identified as the primary cytokine expressed by activated neutrophils/monocytes and macrophages.
evidence: Supported by scRNA-seq analysis of cytokine expression across cell types

claim: A sub-cluster of dermal fibroblasts with preadipocyte signature was identified as a prominent target for IFNγ+ lymphocytes and dermal source for key T cell chemokines CXCL9/10.
source: Furthermore, analysis of skin resident cells identified a sub-cluster of dermal fibroblasts with preadipocyte signature as a prominent target for IFNγ+ lymphocytes and dermal source for key T cell chemokines CXCL9/10.
evidence: Supported by scRNA-seq analysis and immunostaining showing CXCL9/10 expression in preadipocyte-signature dFBs

claim: IFNγ treatment shifted dermal fibroblasts from collagen-producing to CXCL9/10-producing.
source: IFNγ treatment shifted dermal fibroblasts from collagen-producing to CXCL9/10-producing, which promoted T cell polarization toward the type-1 phenotype through a CXCR3-dependent mechanism.
evidence: Supported by in vitro experiments showing IFNγ-induced changes in dFB gene expression

claim: IFNγ-induced CXCL9/10 production by dermal fibroblasts promoted T cell polarization toward the type-1 phenotype through a CXCR3-dependent mechanism.
source: IFNγ treatment shifted dermal fibroblasts from collagen-producing to CXCL9/10-producing, which promoted T cell polarization toward the type-1 phenotype through a CXCR3-dependent mechanism.
evidence: Supported by in vitro co-culture experiments showing CXCR3-dependent effects on T cell IFNγ production

claim: Targeted deletion of Ifngr1 in dermal fibroblasts in mice reduced Cxcl9/10 expression.
source: Furthermore, targeted deletion of Ifngr1 in dermal fibroblasts in mice reduced Cxcl9/10 expression, dermal infiltration of CD8+ T cell, and alleviated ACD inflammation in mice.
evidence: Supported by qRT-PCR data from Ifngr1FB-iKO mice

claim: Targeted deletion of Ifngr1 in dermal fibroblasts in mice reduced dermal infiltration of CD8+ T cell.
source: Furthermore, targeted deletion of Ifngr1 in dermal fibroblasts in mice reduced Cxcl9/10 expression, dermal infiltration of CD8+ T cell, and alleviated ACD inflammation in mice.
evidence: Supported by immunostaining data from Ifngr1FB-iKO mice

claim: Targeted deletion of Ifngr1 in dermal fibroblasts in mice alleviated ACD inflammation.
source: Furthermore, targeted deletion of Ifngr1 in dermal fibroblasts in mice reduced Cxcl9/10 expression, dermal infiltration of CD8+ T cell, and alleviated ACD inflammation in mice.
evidence: Supported by phenotypic and histological data from Ifngr1FB-iKO mice

claim: IFNγ+ CD8+ T cells and CXCL10-producing dermal fibroblasts co-enriched in the dermis of human ACD skin.
source: Finally, we showed that IFNγ+ CD8+ T cells and CXCL10-producing dermal fibroblasts co-enriched in the dermis of human ACD skin.
evidence: Supported by immunostaining data from human ACD skin samples

claim: Dermal fibroblasts play an indispensable role in shaping the development of type-1 skin inflammation through the IFNGR-CXCR3 signaling circuit during ACD pathogenesis.
source: Together, our results define the cell type-specific immune responses in ACD, and recognize an indispensable role of dermal fibroblasts in shaping the development of type-1 skin inflammation through the IFNGR-CXCR3 signaling circuit during ACD pathogenesis.
evidence: Inferred from multiple lines of evidence including scRNA-seq, in vitro experiments, and in vivo knockout studies
